nodes.label: Retention-risk decision-support question
nodes.rationale: Everything else in the project (synthetic data, ML model, Monte Carlo runner, scenario library, root-cause diagnosis, webapp) is deliberately in service of this single question, not a grab-bag of unrelated demos.

nodes.label: ML circularity bug (predicting turnover_risk from its own generating features)
nodes.rationale: The original regressor predicted turnover_risk from level/tenure/salary/team_size, but those targets were a closed-form function of a subset of those same features computed by the same generator — the model was inverting a known formula, not predicting behavior. That symptom of 'no objective' triggered the retention-risk reframe.

nodes.label: Two-populations divergence fix
nodes.rationale: The dataset export (generate_human_factors) and the simulation's per-agent state (HumanProfile.sample()) were independently sampled from similar-but-different formulas. Fixed by HumanProfile.from_row() plus a DatasetBuilder→Organization bridge so 'features from the dataset' and 'labels from forward-simulating that dataset' describe the same population.

nodes.label: Quit-counting bug fix
nodes.rationale: quits_this_tick counted every already-departed employee again on every subsequent tick because EmployeeAgent.step() returns quit=True forever once inactive, making cumulative-quit numbers wildly wrong (764/2000 instead of ~135/2000) until fixed by tracking the active→inactive transition instead of trusting the per-tick flag.

nodes.label: Weak predictive signal diagnosis and calibration
nodes.rationale: The original quit-probability curve and state persistence washed out day-0 signal almost entirely (AUC ~0.55). Diagnosed by comparing an 'oracle' ceiling (AUC using the raw internal risk latent directly) against the achievable model AUC; fixed by raising state persistence and steepening the quit-hazard curve (cubic to power 4). Final realistic AUC ~0.6-0.7.

nodes.label: Targeted-cohort denominator correction
nodes.rationale: Company-wide totals are the wrong denominator for a targeted intervention program: if an intervention touches 120 of 2,000 employees, the other 1,880 employees' quit noise swamps any signal from the 120. compare_intervention tracks outcomes within the targeted cohort specifically.

nodes.label: Locale formatting bug fix (webapp)
nodes.rationale: toLocaleString() without an explicit locale rendered a dollar cost as '$185 236,415' instead of '$185,236' depending on the browser's default locale. Fixed by passing 'en-US' explicitly.

nodes.label: Layoff-vs-voluntary-quit conflation fix
nodes.rationale: Layoff/Termination events deactivated an employee the same way as an organic quit, so an injected layoff could generate a fabricated exit note or silently poison MLOps training data by teaching the model that being laid off looks like voluntary attrition. Fixed by OrganizationModel.organic_quit_ids, which reuses the model's active→inactive transition tracking; events fire before that tracking runs each tick, so an event-deactivated employee never registers as an organic quit.

nodes.label: MLOps promotion gate
nodes.rationale: Promotes a retrained candidate model only if it doesn't regress AUC beyond a tolerance (default 0.02) against a fixed held-out cohort (seed never changes); otherwise leaves production untouched. Every run appends an audit line to models/turnover_promotion_log.jsonl.

nodes.label: At-risk scoring schema gap adapter
nodes.rationale: The trained turnover model expects pulse-trend and rating features the webapp DB doesn't persist. build_scoring_frame substitutes the employee's current wellbeing snapshot for a trailing average, defaults trends to 0 and ratings to a neutral 3.0, and lets department_id contribute nothing to its one-hot slice rather than erroring. Documented, not hidden — the same adapter is what makes real webapp usage collectible as training data.

nodes.label: MLOps live-learning loop
nodes.rationale: Every real simulate/diagnose run (ticks>=6, non-Monte-Carlo) contributes a genuine labeled TurnoverTrainingExample; retrains blend all collected examples in, but the promotion gate's fixed-holdout AUC check still guards production, so live usage can only help or be a no-op, never silently degrade the model. Deliberately not built: fully automatic background retraining and any retention cap on collected examples.

nodes.label: Webapp architecture (thin adapters over one simulation engine)
nodes.rationale: The simulation engine (OrganizationModel, Scenario/Event classes, ML pipeline) has never been rewritten for any of its three interfaces — the dashboard, the CLI scripts, and the FastAPI+React webapp are all thin adapters over the same engine. A deliberate constraint: new interfaces should not require new simulation logic.
